subject: Deal-weighted allocation matrix decision: Lucent / Meridian conflict
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lucent vs Meridian — immediate allocation decision requested

Team,

We have a hard overlap for the same Q3 reserved GPU pool: Lucent (enterprise closed-won, expected start 2027-06-01) and MeridianTech (renewal with uplift pending legal redlines). Both are asking for guaranteed dedicated capacity concurrently and the pool can only satisfy one of the full-reserve configs without impacting our other commitments.

Key facts:
- Lucent: committed to a 36mo Dedicated contract (DEAL-2027-LUC-7321) but final SLA PDF is still in review (attached). Expected onboarding ramp begins 6/1.
- MeridianTech: renewal negotiation; procurement emailed today asking for a firm allocation by 6/5 to proceed with exec approval.
- Current pool: 64 GPUs available for Q3 reserved assignments; Lucent requests 40, Meridian requests 32. If we grant both as-is we exceed available capacity by 8 GPUs.

Immediate ask: we need a short decision framework. I propose a deal-weighted allocation matrix: score by ARR, contractual term, ramp urgency, legal completeness, and strategic tier. Attached is a draft allocation_matrix_q3.xlsx — fill in your scores and return by EOD tomorrow so I can present to Ops.

If we defer, risk: churn/litigation, procurement delays, and SLA escalations. If we pre-emptively cap allocations we may lose Lucent's ramp momentum.

Proposed short-term mitigations:
- Offer Meridian a time-bound soft reservation (12 weeks) with a cap and the option to convert to firm capacity if they sign by 6/15.
- Prioritize Lucent for initial ramp (weeks 1–6) and schedule Meridian after we validate utilization and potential burst windows.
- If both sign firm, trigger a cross-customer compensatory credit (commercial team to approve) rather than over-commit.

Please review the matrix and note hard constraints from sales/legal. I will loop in Ops if we need an emergency capacity carve or cross-region placement.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lucent vs Meridian — immediate allocation decision requested

Adding my notes after a quick run through HubSpot and the Lucent commercial packet.

- Lucent ARR (projected year 1): $1.45M, committed technical onboarding windows in June. Legal has one open item (data locality in EU clause) but commercial is comfortable with conditional start.
- Meridian ARR (current renewal): $620k, they have an escrow-style clause in procurement that needs our counter-signed exhibits. Procurement pressure is high; if we delay, they will seek alternatives.

Scoring suggestion (simple 0–5 each):
- ARR: Lucent 5 / Meridian 3
- Term length: Lucent 5 (36mo) / Meridian 2 (12mo)
- Ramp urgency: Lucent 4 / Meridian 5 (procurement deadline)
- Legal completeness: Lucent 3 / Meridian 2
- Strategic tier (reference customers): Lucent 4 / Meridian 3

Preliminary weighted total favors Lucent by ~6 points. I support prioritizing Lucent for initial firm reservation but we should offer Meridian a convert-option with explicit timelines and a nominal reservation fee to hold capacity. That preserves revenue upside and reduces churn risk.

I updated allocation_matrix_q3.xlsx (tab: scores) — see attachment.

-karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 13:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lucent vs Meridian — immediate allocation decision requested

Thanks — good work pulling the numbers. A few operational / commercial constraints from my side: 

1) SLA commitments: if we promise Lucent the full 40 GPUs by 6/1 we must ensure the canary stack and burn-in completes by 5/28. Ops needs 48 hours per rack for validation. That compresses the timeline a lot.
2) Credit policy: Marketing/Finance have capped one-off goodwill credits at 10% MRR equivalent for allocation slip. Anything above requires director-level approval.
3) Cross-region option: We can offer Meridian a regionally split reservation (e.g., 16 us-west + 8 us-east), but that increases network egress complexity.

Recommendation: Approve Lucent for initial firm allocation of 36 GPUs now (reserve 4 as burst capacity). Offer Meridian a conditional reservation: 24 firm + 8 soft-convert for 30 total if signed by 6/12. Include a reservation fee of 7.5% ARR for the soft portion to compensate.

If Ops cannot validate Lucent by 5/28, we downgrade to the soft window and revert to the conditional reservation plan. Ben, can you confirm the ops validation SLA and whether cross-region placement is feasible without violating Lucent's EU clause?

-Marissa
From: Andrew Zhou <andrew.zhou@lucent.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 07:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal-weighted allocation matrix decision: Lucent / Meridian conflict

Tessa / Karthik,

Appreciate the quick coordination. From Lucent's side: we are willing to be flexible on a 36 GPU firm start with a 4 GPU burst pool, provided you waive any first-30-day SLA credits and guarantee onboarding support. Legal will finalize the EU data locality amendment by EOD Monday (6/23), but we need the operational start on 6/1 to meet our product launch.

If Redwood requires the 48-hour validation window, we can arrange remote validation runs and provide a small engineering team for a two-day joint burn-in to accelerate. Lucent prefers the 3-year term and will not accept regionally split capacity that violates data locality.

Please confirm and send the updated exhibit.

Thanks,
Andrew
Andrew Zhou
Head of Cloud Ops — Lucent AI
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Andrew Zhou <andrew.zhou@lucent.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final alignment: allocation decision and next steps

All,

Summary and decision based on scoring, Ops constraints, and Lucent's willingness to assist with validation:
- Lucent: allocate 36 GPUs firm (reserve 4 for burst). Can begin on 6/1 contingent on joint burn-in validation (remote assistance accepted). Legal to deliver EU amendment by 6/23; hold firm allocation pending receipt but proceed with onboarding prep.
- MeridianTech: offer conditional reservation of 24 firm + 8 soft-convert (30 total) if signed by 6/12. Apply a 7.5% reservation fee for soft capacity; convert to standard billing upon signature.
- Credits: any SLA credit for the first 30 days is waived for Lucent as part of the commercial concession in exchange for commitment language in the exhibit. Larger credit requests escalate to director approval.
- Ops: Ben confirmed we can meet validation if Lucent provides engineers for the two-day remote burn-in; cross-region placement is not acceptable for Lucent due to data locality.

Next steps (owners / ETA):
- Legal: finalize Lucent EU exhibit and send for signature — owner: Karthik / Legal — ETA: 2027-05-24 EOD.
- Finance/RevOps: prepare reservation invoice for Meridian soft-reserve — owner: Marissa — ETA: 2027-05-24 EOD.
- Ops: schedule joint remote burn-in with Lucent engineers week of 5/24 — owner: Ben — ETA: calendar invites out by 5/21 EOD.
- Sales: notify Meridian contact of conditional reservation and terms — owner: Karthik — ETA: 2027-05-21 EOD.

I'll update the HubSpot deal and upload the signed exhibits when they arrive. If anything changes (legal redlines or Ops capacity hits), we re-open this thread immediately.

Thanks everyone for moving quickly.

Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
